name: narration_comments
description: Comments that narrate code flow with phrases like 'Step 1:', 'First,', 'Now we', 'Next,' immediately before code that does exactly what the comment says.
positive_indicators: '// Step 1: Initialize the list' above 'const results: Item[] = []'
'// Now we loop through each item' above 'for (const item of items) {'
'// First, get the user' above 'const user = getUser(id)'
'// Next, validate the input' above 'validate(input)'
negative_indicators: '// Retry with exponential backoff to handle rate limits' (explains WHY)
'// HACK: workaround for bug #1234' (provides context)
'// NOTE: order matters here due to dependency' (non-obvious insight)

name: echo_docstrings
description: JSDoc or block comments that only restate the function name in sentence form without adding parameter details, return values, edge cases, or context.
positive_indicators: 'function getUser(id: string)' with '/** Gets the user. */'
'function calculateTotal()' with '/** Calculates the total. */'
'function processData(data: unknown)' with '/** Processes the data. */'
negative_indicators: JSDoc that names units, empty-list behavior, or thrown errors
'/** Sum item prices with tax. Rounds to 2 decimal places. Empty list returns 0. */'
'/** Transform the raw API body for the UI. Call after parseResponse(). */'

name: entry_exit_logging
description: Logging statements at function entry/exit in short functions (<20 lines) that add no diagnostic value.
positive_indicators: 'console.log("Entering processItem")' at start of a 5-line function
'console.info("Starting...")' and 'console.info("Done.")' wrapping trivial logic
'console.log("function called")' at function entry
negative_indicators: Logging in functions that make external calls or I/O
Logging with actual variable values for debugging
Logging in error paths or catch blocks

name: class_prefix_in_members
description: Class or interface members that redundantly include the type name as a prefix, when the surrounding type already provides that information.
positive_indicators: 'class User { userId; userName; userEmail }'
'interface Order { orderItems; orderTotal; orderDate }'
'type Config = { configPath: string; configValues: Record<string, string> }'
negative_indicators: 'class User { id; name; email }'
'interface Order { items; total; date }'
'type Config = { path: string; values: Record<string, string> }'

name: delegation_only_class
description: Classes or objects where every method simply delegates to an underlying object's method of the same name, adding no behavior.
positive_indicators: 'class Wrapper { save() { return this.inner.save() } }'
Every method is 'return this.inner.methodName(...)'
A facade that mirrors the wrapped interface exactly
negative_indicators: 'save() { this.validate(); return this.inner.save() }' (adds a step)
'save() { const r = this.inner.save(); log(r); return r }'
'getItems(limit?: number) { return this.inner.fetchAll().slice(0, limit) }'

name: lonely_interface
description: An interface or abstract class with exactly one implementing class in the entire codebase.
positive_indicators: 'interface UserRepository' with only 'class PgUserRepository implements UserRepository'
'interface DataSource' with only one implementor
'type Validator = { parse(v: unknown): T }' with one object
negative_indicators: Interface with multiple implementations
Interface from a library you implement
Interface used as a test double where tests exist

name: one_subclass_hierarchy
description: An abstract base class with exactly one concrete subclass, where the abstraction provides no benefit.
positive_indicators: 'abstract class Processor' with only 'class ConcreteProcessor extends Processor'
'class BaseHandler' with only 'class RequestHandler extends BaseHandler'
negative_indicators: Base class with multiple subclasses
Base class that is a framework extension point
Base class shared across modules

name: single_entry_registry
description: A registry, map, or dispatch table containing only one entry, negating the purpose of the pattern.
positive_indicators: 'const handlers = { default: DefaultHandler }'
'const STRATEGIES = { main: MainStrategy }'
'registry.set("only", impl)'
negative_indicators: Registry with multiple entries
Registry populated dynamically at runtime
Registry designed for user extension

name: factory_returns_constant
description: Factory function or class that always returns the same concrete type, with no conditionals or configuration affecting the result.
positive_indicators: 'function createService() { return new ConcreteService() }'
'function getHandler(): Handler { return new DefaultHandler() }'
negative_indicators: Factory that switches on a type parameter
Factory that reads configuration to decide type
Factory that returns different types based on input

name: strategy_never_varies
description: Strategy pattern where the strategy field is set once and never changed, injected, or selected dynamically.
positive_indicators: 'private readonly strategy = new DefaultStrategy()' never reassigned
Strategy field with no setter, always the same value
negative_indicators: Strategy passed as a constructor parameter
Strategy selected from configuration
Strategy changed at runtime

name: interface_per_class
description: Every concrete class has a corresponding interface, even when only one implementation exists and no mocking is needed.
positive_indicators: 'interface UserService' paired with only 'class UserServiceImpl'
1:1 interface-to-class ratio throughout the codebase
negative_indicators: Interfaces with multiple implementations
Interfaces used for test doubles with actual test files
Interfaces required by a dependency-injection framework

name: cache_for_literals
description: Memoization or caching applied to functions that only perform simple arithmetic, string operations, or return constants.
positive_indicators: 'useMemo(() => a + b, [a, b])'
A Map cache around 'function add(a, b) { return a + b }'
Memoizing a pure O(1) computation
negative_indicators: Caching functions that make I/O or network calls
Caching expensive parsing or sorting
Caching results of database queries

name: parallel_small_collection
description: Using worker threads or Promise.all parallelism for processing small collections where overhead exceeds benefit.
positive_indicators: 'Promise.all(items.map(...))' for 2-3 synchronous operations
Worker threads to process a list of 5 items
async/await for CPU-bound work on small data
negative_indicators: Parallel I/O (multiple network requests)
Parallel processing of large datasets
Parallel work where each item is slow I/O

name: lazy_always_accessed
description: Lazy initialization for values that are unconditionally accessed every time the containing object is used.
positive_indicators: A lazy getter that every method then calls
'getInstance()' called on every use of the class
negative_indicators: Lazy init for expensive resources that might not be needed
Lazy init for optional features
Lazy init to break circular imports

name: redundant_null_check
description: Checking the same variable for null, undefined, or empty multiple times in close proximity (within 10 lines), or after already establishing it is valid.
positive_indicators: 'if (user) { ... if (user != null) {'
'if (items) { for (const item of items) { if (item) {'
negative_indicators: Null check after reassignment
Null check in different branches
Null check where the value could have changed
A null or undefined guard when the declared type includes null or undefined
'const v = map.get(k); if (v == null) continue' because Map.get returns T | undefined
'const x = arr.find(pred); if (x == null)' because find returns T | undefined
'items[i] == null' under noUncheckedIndexedAccess, where indexed access is T | undefined
Flag only when the type already excludes null and undefined, or the same value was just checked

name: default_on_required_field
description: Using nullish coalescing (??, ?.) or '|| default' on values that come from constructors, required parameters, or guaranteed sources.
positive_indicators: 'this.name ?? "unknown"' when name is a required constructor param
'user?.id' when user comes from an authenticated session
'config.timeout || 30' when config is validated at startup
negative_indicators: Default on optional parameters
Default on values from external sources (API, user input)
Default on values that could legitimately be missing
'balances.get(name) ?? 0' when Map.get is typed T | undefined, including when name came from balances.keys()
'arr[i] ?? fallback' under noUncheckedIndexedAccess, where indexed access is T | undefined
'arr.find(pred) ?? fallback' because find returns T | undefined
Default on an optional property or a value whose declared type includes null or undefined. Flag only when the type already excludes null and undefined, or the same value was just checked

name: silent_truncation
description: Slicing or truncating data to fit limits without logging, validating, or otherwise indicating data loss occurred.
positive_indicators: 'name.slice(0, 50)' without a length check or warning
'items.slice(0, MAX)' silently dropping items
negative_indicators: Truncation with a log when data is cut
Truncation with validation that input fits
Truncation documented as expected behavior in the spec

name: silent_resource_creation
description: Automatically creating missing resources (directories, files) without logging or warning that creation occurred.
positive_indicators: 'mkdirSync(path, { recursive: true })' without logging
'if (!existsSync(f)) writeFileSync(f, "")'
negative_indicators: Resource creation with logging
Resource creation in an explicit setup function
Resource creation documented in the spec

name: unrequested_features
description: Code implements features, flags, options, or capabilities not mentioned anywhere in the spec. Compare implemented functionality against spec requirements.
positive_indicators: CLI flags like --verbose, --dry-run, --config not in the spec
Output format options (JSON, XML) when the spec asks for one
Optional parameters for customization the spec does not mention
negative_indicators: Features explicitly requested in the spec
Features required for basic functionality implied by the spec
Standard error handling

name: handling_excluded_cases
description: Code handles edge cases or inputs that the spec explicitly says will not occur, can be assumed valid, or are out of scope.
positive_indicators: Validation for inputs the spec says are always valid
Empty/null checks when the spec guarantees non-empty
Error handling for cases the spec says will not happen
negative_indicators: Handling cases the spec says MUST be handled
Reasonable defensive coding for undefined spec areas
Validation at true system boundaries

name: scaffold_remnants
description: Generated scaffolding left half-implemented, adding noise without behavior.
positive_indicators: Auto-generated files with TODO bodies
Routes or commands registered that throw or return a placeholder
Placeholder tests that always pass or are skipped
negative_indicators: Generated stubs that were fully implemented
Scaffolding kept only in a documented template directory

name: stub_implementations
description: Functions or methods that return placeholders instead of real behavior.
positive_indicators: 'return undefined // TODO' in business logic
'throw new Error("not implemented")' in code that should run
Methods that always return hardcoded defaults unrelated to inputs
negative_indicators: Abstract members meant to be overridden
Temporary stubs clearly marked and skipped in wiring

name: unnecessary_monadic_wrappers
description: Result/Option wrappers on values that are never optional, or errors that still crash.
positive_indicators: Result<T, E> used but errors are immediately unwrapped
Optional around values guaranteed by construction
map/flatMap chains replacing a simple if/throw
negative_indicators: Result/Option used to model real absence or recoverable errors
Wrappers that simplify complex branching

name: unnecessary_type_wrappers
description: Wrapper classes or types around primitives with no validation or behavior.
positive_indicators: 'type UserId = { value: string }' used only to pass strings through
Newtypes immediately unwrapped at API boundaries
Getters/setters only for a single primitive
negative_indicators: Wrappers enforcing invariants or formatting
Types that carry domain behavior (methods, validation)

name: nested_async_flows
description: Async callbacks or promises nested inside each other, obscuring execution order.
positive_indicators: 'fetch().then(r => r.json().then(body => fetch(body.url).then(...)))' three levels deep
Callbacks defined inside async handlers inside other callbacks
negative_indicators: Flat async/await with clear sequencing
Promise chains that stay linear and readable

name: inline_state_machines
description: Implicit state machines implemented by mutating a 'state' variable across branches.
positive_indicators: 'let state = "init"; if (x) state = "running"; ...' scattered across a function
'let isStarted = false; let isComplete = false; let hasError = false' toggled in 5+ places
negative_indicators: Explicit transition tables or discriminated unions with clear edges
State encapsulated in a dedicated object or reducer

name: boolean_success_flags
description: Functions returning success booleans instead of throwing or returning rich errors.
positive_indicators: '[result, ok]' tuples where ok must be checked
Methods returning true/false with no error detail
APIs that swallow errors and only return a status
negative_indicators: 'function contains(item) { return this.set.has(item) }' (membership)
throw with a specific error
A Result type with a useful error

name: sentinel_values_as_errors
description: Using magic values to signal errors instead of explicit error handling.
positive_indicators: Return -1, '', or 0 to mean 'not found' or 'error'
null/undefined used to mean both 'missing' and 'error'
Special IDs like 0 meaning 'no user'
negative_indicators: Documented sentinel values at well-defined boundaries
Distinct error types or thrown errors

name: error_message_destruction
description: Replacing specific errors with generic messages, hiding root cause details.
positive_indicators: catch then 'throw new Error("Invalid input")'
Returning '{ error: true }' without message or field details
'console.error("An error occurred")' with no cause
negative_indicators: Sanitizing sensitive details while keeping actionable info
Adding context while preserving the original message

name: retry_loops_hiding_failures
description: Retries that discard intermediate failures, hiding flakiness or root causes.
positive_indicators: 'for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) { try { return await doIt() } catch { } }'
Retry helper with no on-failure logging
A while loop retrying indefinitely without backoff or trace
negative_indicators: Retries with logged attempts and a surfaced final error
Backoff that records failures

name: lenient_parsing
description: Parsers that accept malformed input by guessing or defaulting, hiding producer bugs.
positive_indicators: 'Number(value) || 0' on untrusted input
Date parsing that tries many formats silently
'JSON.parse' in try/catch returning {} with no error
negative_indicators: Strict parsing that fails fast on bad data
Leniency with logging when accepting loose input

name: type_coercion_hiding_mismatches
description: Implicit or explicit coercion that makes wrong types pass silently.
positive_indicators: 'String(id)' to accept any input
Loose equality like 'x == "1"' matching numbers
'Number(value)' without validating numeric input
negative_indicators: Explicit validation with clear errors on type mismatch
Coercion only in user-facing input layers with logging

name: defensive_cloning_hiding_mutation
description: Cloning inputs/outputs everywhere to hide unintended mutation instead of fixing it.
positive_indicators: '{...obj}' or 'structuredClone' at every function entry
Getters that always return deep copies of internal state
Clone before and after trivial operations
negative_indicators: Cloning around known mutating calls to contain side effects
Immutability at boundaries to prevent mutation bugs

name: handrolled_standard_operations
description: Reimplementing common library or language utilities instead of using built-ins.
positive_indicators: Manual index loops to map/filter/trim when built-ins exist
Custom reduce for a simple sum
Home-grown retry/backoff when a library helper exists
negative_indicators: Custom logic because built-ins lack needed behavior
Performance-tuned implementations with evidence

name: log_level_hiding
description: Logging important diagnostics at levels that are filtered out in production, or only via debug prints.
positive_indicators: Exceptions logged only with console.debug
Request errors logged at a level typically disabled
negative_indicators: Errors logged with console.error where they are visible
Debug logging gated by config but with a fallback

name: implicit_default_parameters
description: Behavior-changing parameters defaulted in code so callers trigger modes without realizing.
positive_indicators: Important options with defaults buried in function signatures
Flags like 'cache = true, limit = 1000' that silently alter behavior
Mode parameters defaulting to a non-neutral behavior
negative_indicators: Defaults documented and surfaced at call sites
Defaults that are neutral no-op behaviors

name: silent_fallbacks
description: Fallback chains that hide which path succeeded, masking primary failures.
positive_indicators: try primary then secondary with no logging
'const value = a ?? b ?? c' with no trace of source
Config/env resolution with multiple tiers and no visibility
negative_indicators: Fallbacks that log which source was used
Explicit propagation of which path handled the request

name: auto_correction_without_warning
description: Silently fixing bad config/input (clamping, auto-creating resources) instead of failing or warning.
positive_indicators: Clamping timeouts or ranges without logging
auto-mkdir for missing paths in core logic
Normalizing invalid options to defaults quietly
negative_indicators: Corrections logged with clear visibility
Validation errors raised for invalid inputs

name: null_coalescing_abuse
description: Using ?? or || defaults on values that should never be null, hiding real bugs.
positive_indicators: Required config/env vars defaulted to hardcoded values
'user?.id ?? "unknown"' on required fields
Chaining ?. on objects that must exist by spec
negative_indicators: Defaults only on truly optional fields
Guarded access at external input boundaries
'map.get(k) ?? 0' when Map.get is typed T | undefined, including when k came from the same map's keys()
'obj[k] ?? 0' under noUncheckedIndexedAccess
'find(...) ?? default' because find returns T | undefined
?? or || on T | null | undefined, including optional fields. Flag only when the type already excludes null and undefined, or the same value was just checked

name: stringly_typed_logic
description: Using raw strings for modes, types, or states instead of unions or constants.
positive_indicators: Status/mode comparisons on repeated string literals
Dispatch on string names of actions
String unions used where a discriminated union would be clearer
negative_indicators: Typed unions or enums referenced consistently
Strings only at I/O boundaries with conversion to types

name: ignoring_return_values
description: Calling functions where return values matter but are unused, risking missed errors or results.
positive_indicators: 'repo.save(user)' without checking result/status
API calls whose responses are dropped
A helper returning an updated object that is ignored
negative_indicators: Explicitly fire-and-forget calls documented as such
Deliberate ignore because the return is irrelevant

name: validation_mismatch
description: Validation rules that contradict or misalign with the spec or domain.
positive_indicators: Rejecting inputs the spec allows
Allowing inputs the spec forbids
Validation messages that do not match enforced rules
negative_indicators: Validation logic matching documented requirements
Flexible validation explicitly allowed by the spec

name: validation_theater
description: Validation code that runs but does not change outcomes (no throws, ignores failures).
positive_indicators: 'validate()' return value ignored
Errors collected but never surfaced
Checks that only log but proceed on invalid data
negative_indicators: 'const errors = validate(data); if (errors.length) throw ...'
Returning an error object to the caller
Visible warnings when proceeding

name: domain_blind_normalization
description: Normalization that discards domain meaning, corrupting data silently.
positive_indicators: Lowercasing IDs that are case-sensitive
Truncating fields without domain rules
Stripping characters that carry meaning (leading zeros)
negative_indicators: Normalization aligned with domain rules (emails case-folded locally)
Validation that rejects out-of-domain formats instead of altering them

name: unchecked_parse_typing
description: Assigning JSON.parse or Response.json() to a typed variable, or using a typed assertion on parse, with no runtime check that the value matches the type.
positive_indicators: 'const user: User = await res.json()'
'const data = JSON.parse(text) as Config'
'const body: Payload = JSON.parse(raw)'
negative_indicators: Parse to unknown, then a type guard or schema parse
A runtime check of required fields before the value is used as T

name: type_guard_theater
description: A user-defined type predicate that does not check the properties it claims, so a failed runtime value still narrows to the type.
positive_indicators: 'function isUser(v: unknown): v is User { return true }'
'function isUser(v: unknown): v is User { return typeof v === "object" && v !== null }' with no field checks
'return v as User' inside a predicate
negative_indicators: A predicate that checks each claimed field and nested shape
A schema parse that infers the type

name: redundant_undefined_checks
description: Guards for undefined, null, or missing keys on values the types already prove present (required fields, non-optional parameters, narrowed unions).
positive_indicators: 'if (user.name === undefined)' when name is typed string
'opts.limit ?? 10' when limit is a required number
'if (items)' when items is T[]
negative_indicators: Guards on T | undefined or optional properties
Guards on values that just arrived from unknown/external input
'map.get(k) ?? 0' or 'if (map.get(k) === undefined)' because Map.get returns T | undefined
'items[i]' guarded when noUncheckedIndexedAccess types it as T | undefined
'arr.find(...)' guarded because find returns T | undefined
Flag only when the type already excludes undefined, or the same value was just checked

name: single_use_abstraction
description: A hook, component, or helper that is used once and adds only indirection, with no extra behavior, types, or test seam.
positive_indicators: 'function useFormatDate' called from one site and returning a one-line format

'function CardWrapper({ children }) { return
{children}
}' used once
A helper that only forwards to another function with the same arguments
negative_indicators: Used in two or more places
Used once but hides real branching, I/O, or a boundary parse

name: stale_response_race
description: Async results applied to state or the DOM without guarding against out-of-order responses when the request key can change.
positive_indicators: 'useEffect(() => { load(id).then(setData) }, [id])' with no cancelled flag or AbortController
'fetch(url).then(r => r.json()).then(setItems)' in an effect without cleanup
negative_indicators: AbortController in the effect cleanup
'let cancelled = false' with a cleanup that sets it and a check before setState
A query library that keys the result to the request

name: effect_for_derived_data
description: A useEffect that writes state derived from props, other state, or render-time values, instead of computing the value during render.
positive_indicators: 'useEffect(() => setFullName(first + last), [first, last])'
'useEffect(() => setVisible(items.filter(isOn)), [items])'
setState inside an effect whose deps are the inputs of a pure calculation
negative_indicators: Derived values computed during render
An effect that syncs with an external system (document title, subscription, network)

name: manual_async_status
description: Local loading, error, or idle booleans (or a status enum in useState) that duplicate what a query or form library already tracks.
positive_indicators: 'const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)' around a fetch
'const [error, setError] = useState(false)' plus a loading flag
'useState<"idle" | "loading" | "error">' set by hand around useEffect fetch
negative_indicators: Status from useQuery or a similar library
No local loading copy because the UI reads the query

name: state_copy_of_props_or_items
description: Copying props or fetched items into useState so the UI reads a stale local copy instead of the source value.
positive_indicators: 'const [items, setItems] = useState(props.items)'
'useEffect(() => setItems(props.items), [props.items])'
'const [list, setList] = useState(items)' when items is already state or query data
negative_indicators: Rendering props.items or query data directly
A key on the component that remounts when the identity changes
